prompt.en: Build the whole way first, then press go.
prompt.ar: اِبْنِ الطَّرِيقَ كُلَّهُ أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ اضْغَطْ اِنْطَلِق.

hint1.en: Watch where it stopped. What would you change?

hint2.en: Start with the glowing arrow, then keep going.

model.en: Watch the whole way through once. Then you drive it.
model.ar: شَاهِدِ الطَّرِيقَ كُلَّهُ مَرَّةً. ثُمَّ قُدْهَا أَنْت.

success.en: Both baskets delivered, and nothing tipped over.

payload._comment: The only activity in this chapter where the child commits to a whole plan before seeing any of it happen. Everything else answers one tap at a time. Predict, run, watch, revise is the thing being practised, which is why the cart drives the child's program in full — including a wrong one — before anything is judged: watching what your plan did IS the lesson, and telling them the answer while the cart was still moving would take it away.
payload._commandComment: Absolute arrows, not turn-and-go. A three-year-old can read 'that way' straight off the screen; 'turn left, then forward' asks them to hold a heading in mind and rotate it, which is a later skill. The engine simulates both, so the harder set is a one-word content change when a later Adventure wants it. The arrows are spatial rather than textual, so they are NOT mirrored in Arabic — a mirrored arrow would drive the cart the wrong way.

label.en: The fruit stall is at the end of the lane. A barrel is in the way.
label.ar: كُشْكُ الفَاكِهَةِ فِي آخِرِ المَمَرّ. وَهُنَاكَ بِرْمِيلٌ يَسُدُّ الطَّرِيق.

revealLine.en: The apples are there. One more basket to go.

label.en: Now the vegetable stall, down at the corner. Mind the crates.
label.ar: وَالآنَ كُشْكُ الخُضَارِ عِنْدَ الزَّاوِيَة. اِنْتَبِهْ لِلصَّنَادِيق.

revealLine.en: Delivered. Both stalls have what they were waiting for.
revealLine.ar: تَمَّ التَّوْصِيل. صَارَ لَدَى الكُشْكَيْنِ مَا كَانَا يَنْتَظِرَانِه.
